discovery: Photonic crystals: the photonic band gap concept and its realization for controlling light emission and confinement
motivation: In 1987 Yablonovitch and John independently showed that periodic dielectric structures can open a photonic band gap, a frequency range in which light cannot propagate. Yablonovitch proposed it to inhibit spontaneous emission; John showed it enables strong localization of light. Yablonovitch then demonstrated the first three-dimensional band gap experimentally. The idea moved control of light–matter interaction from the material to the structure, and it gave rise to modern nanophotonics. Noda turned the concept into rigorous devices: full control of spontaneous emission, ultrahigh-Q nanocavities in photonic-crystal slabs, and the photonic-crystal surface-emitting laser. That laser now delivers watt-class, single-mode, high-brightness output and has reached industry. Together these contributions form a field-defining discovery, from fundamental band-gap physics to quantum light sources, slow light, energy-efficient on-chip lasers and extreme light confinement. Its importance is comparable to that of the semiconductor heterostructure.
